title: Tertiary lymphoid structures harbour stem-like tumour-specific T cells.
data_url: https://singlecell.broadinstitute.org/single_cell/study/SCP3155 (spatial data, login required); dbGaP study uid 2612223 (controlled access, linked from PubMed 42486979)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (subscription-only, no PubMed Central ID, no supplementary files). NCBI link-out from PubMed 42486979 goes only to dbGaP (controlled-access human data archive), uid 2612223; no GEO, SRA, BioProject or BioSample links exist. I retrieved the full file manifest of Broad Single Cell Portal study SCP3155 via its public JSON interface: 140 files, 223.0 GB total, of which 14 are raw sequencing files (fastq.gz, 7.3-26.0 GB each, 222.0 GB combined) and only 1.04 GB is processed (19 AnnData .h5ad files of 0.09-0.50 MB, 19 Seurat .Rds files of 2.3-35.9 MB, 19 Slide-seq spatial count matrices of 6-42 MB, and one 209 MB Bead_level_supplementary_table.csv), covering 19 tissue slides (pucks) from 7 tumour samples. Every download route returned an authentication error: per-file download 401, per-file stream 401, bulk-download summary 401, and the /data/public/ path 500. The Nature article page itself 303-redirects to an identity-provider login.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All biology and all counts about the actual experiment come from the abstract alone: 24 treatment-naive renal cell carcinoma (a kidney cancer) tumours profiled, 554 expanded T cell clonotypes screened for what they recognise, 82 T cell receptors found reactive to tumour cells or kidney-cancer antigens, 12% of tumour-specific clonotypes enriched in tertiary lymphoid structures (immune cell clusters inside tumours), and 60 further tumours analysed spatially. I could not see the data availability statement, the methods, or any supplementary table, so I never saw a single row or column of the reactivity labels.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified by trying it. The only NCBI deposit is a dbGaP study (uid 2612223), which needs a formal data access application. The spatial deposit SCP3155 is flagged public but all four download endpoints refuse without a signed-in account (HTTP 401; the /data/public/ route gives 500). The paper is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy and no Europe PMC supplementary files, so the supplementary tables holding the T cell reactivity labels are behind the paywall too.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed; stopped at A1. The label (is this T cell receptor tumour-reactive, yes/no) is almost certainly a supplementary-table column, but I never saw the table.

a5_enough_rows.note: Likely a second failure even with access. The abstract's screening unit is 554 T cell clonotypes from only 6 tumours, with 82 positives; the tumour-level unit is 24 (plus 60 independent) tumours, far under the ~400-row floor for classification, and 6 patients means almost no independent groups.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.0 GB processed spatial files (the other 222.0 GB are raw sequencing reads we would never download)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size alone would be fine if the files could be fetched.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable: no accessible data file to count against the abstract's numbers.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed; stopped at A1. The abstract implies a real laboratory reactivity screen, which would be good provenance, but note the macrophage phenotype and tumour-reactivity calls in the 60-tumour cohort are described as 'inferred' and 'putative', i.e. computational, not measured.

backbone.name: Not assessed (stopped at A1); a T cell receptor language model such as TCR-BERT or a single-cell model such as scGPT would have been the natural choice

integration.partner_dataset: VDJdb and McPAS-TCR, public catalogues of T cell receptor sequences with known targets
integration.join_key: T cell receptor CDR3 amino acid sequence plus V and J gene names
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can tumour-reactive T cell receptors be told apart from virus-reactive ones by sequence and expression alone? Unanswerable here because the receptor sequences and their reactivity calls are not obtainable.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the measurements that would be modelled are in a controlled-access archive and a login-walled portal, so nothing can be verified or trained on.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a T cell's receptor sequence and gene activity to predict whether it recognises the patient's own tumour.
plain_idea.train_on: What each example would be: one expanded T cell clonotype (a family of identical T cells) from a kidney tumour, described by its receptor sequence and its single-cell gene expression. The paper reports 554 such clonotypes from 6 tumours; I verified no count myself.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no call on tumour reactivity. The true answer comes from the paper's laboratory screen, in which T cells were exposed to the patient's own tumour cells or kidney-cancer antigens and their activation measured; the abstract says 82 of 554 were reactive.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cell-therapy groups must currently run slow, patient-specific laboratory screens to pick which T cell receptors to put into a therapy; a sequence-based filter would cut that work. Even a failure would quantify how far receptor sequence alone can go.

ml_idea: Predict tumour reactivity of a T cell clonotype from its receptor sequence plus its single-cell expression profile, and separately predict whether a clonotype sits inside a tertiary lymphoid structure from its expression. Both are blocked: the reactivity labels are in paywalled supplementary tables, the single-cell data is in dbGaP (needs an access application), and the spatial data on the Broad Single Cell Portal needs a login to download. Sample size would also be marginal: 554 clonotypes from 6 patients, 24 tumours.

effort.compute_note: Only the deposit manifest was measurable: 1.04 GB of processed spatial files versus 222.0 GB of raw reads. No timing was done because no file could be opened.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Request one small file from the Single Cell Portal deposit without logging in (it returns HTTP 401) and check whether the linked dbGaP study uid 2612223 is open access (it is not). Two commands, under a minute, and the project is dead.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails on verified evidence: the single-cell and T cell receptor data sit in dbGaP behind an access application, every download route for the spatial deposit SCP3155 returns an authentication error, and the paper plus its supplementary tables are subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy, so the reactivity labels cannot be obtained at all. Even with full access, A5 would likely fail too, since the labelled unit is 554 clonotypes from 6 patients and the tumour-level unit is 24 samples.
